best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

Niche option used in tthe Jingran/Mortefi/Lupa team. Grants a Shield on cast which can activate Jingran's passive for a lot of Fusion DMG Bonus gained upon casting his Intro. Usually Swap Cancelled at the end of Mortefi's rotation.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect which triggers when the wearer of this set critically strikes with a Coordinated attack - this effect grants the on field Resonator an ATK% boost regardless if they're the wearer of the set or not. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers a 40% unconditional Coordinated Attack DMG% boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Coordinated Attack-focused resonators looking to use the 5P Empyrean Anthem Echo set bonus.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Mortefi is a 4-star Fusion Pistol buffer character who specializes in buffing Heavy Attack damage. He also has access to some Coordinated Attacks and is well-known for being one of the best F2P characters since the game's release.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Mortefi's rotation goal is to get his Outro off as quickly as physically possible. To do this, he needs to charge up his Forte gauge, which allows him to cast a Forte Skill that generates a good amount of Concerto and deals some damage. He charges this Forte gauge up through his Intro, Basic Attacks, and Skill.

To charge it as quickly as possible, Mortefi should cast his Skill before any Basic Attacks. An Intro and a Skill already charge up a full Forte gauge, so he can cast a Forte Skill, while within 5s after casting his base Skill, Mortefi generates extra Forte through his Basic Attacks. A full Basic Attack string becomes enough for his next Forte Skill to be available, and at that point he has enough Concerto Energy to Outro if his Ultimate is also cast.

Speaking of his Ultimate, at S6 it gives an extra 20% ATK to the whole party on cast for 20s, it deals a bit of damage, and also it enables Mortefi to fire Coordinated Attacks at the enemy for 10 (S0) to 17 (S4) seconds. These Coordinated Attacks are triggered once by Basic Attack casts, twice by Heavy Attack casts, and also twice by Skill casts at S1. Overall, this allows Mortefi to fire off a good amount of Coordinated Attacks regardless of who he is paired with, but he does scale a bit better with Heavy Attack casters in this regard.

Finally, his Outro gives the next character 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification for 14s, expiring on swap. This is the main buff in his kit and makes or breaks his synergies. Mortefi's passives give him a bit of extra personal damage, not much to explain there.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: In the meta, Mortefi is super easy to understand. He's completely one-dimensional and restricted to buffing Heavy Attackers, mostly through his Outro. He's simple, but effective in his role. As a F2P buffing character, he sports a nice amount of generalist buffs: 38% Heavy DMG Amplification, and up to 52.5% ATK and 12% DMG Bonus with Moonlit Clouds, S6, and Static Mist all factored in.

Indeed, his best weapon being a permanent banner one gives him a good amount of usability in all endgame content alongside Heavy Attack damage dealers like Jingran, Yangyang: Xuanling, Augusta, or even his on-release partner Jiyan. Team DPS can vary pretty wildly based on how modern the damage dealer that he pairs with is. However, the more Heavy Attack damage dealers that release, the more Mortefi gains staying power, not as a best in slot option, but as a F2P replacement for all future Heavy Attackers to come.

In conclusion, Mortefi is a simple Heavy Attack buffer who can act as a potent buffer for all your Heavy Attack damage dealers. While never ideal in those teams, he can always replace a limited 5-star character to buff your DPS. If you're in a pinch for teammates or have a modern enough DPS where you don't need their dedicated Supports to clear endgame, Mortefi is a great choice, and is likely to remain that way in the future as long as Heavy Attack DPS characters release.

synergies.commentary: Mortefi is by far the best F2P-accessible option for her as he provides a massive 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplify on his Outro, which he accesses quickly and easily while retaining solid off-field personal damage via his Ultimate's Marcato Coordinated Attacks. As a pistol user, he additionally has access to an extra ATK% buff from the Static Mist weapon and he has an extra ATK% buff with his S6 as well, making him one of the best options by far.

As one of Galbrena's best partners, Mortefi provides 38% Heavy Attack DMG Amplify on his Outro which is one of Galbrena's 2 main damage types. Additionally, he can wield Moonlit Clouds and the Static Mist pistol for a ton of ATK% and DMG% buffing. On top of his fast rotation and solid personal damage, he makes for a fantastic Galbrena teammate in general, particularly with Lupa in a Mono Fusion setup.

Mortefi is Jiyan's tailor-made partner. Via his Echo Sets, his S6 and Static Mist, Mortefi can give lots of ATK% buffs, but most importantly he amplifies Jiyan's main damage type, Heavy ATK DMG, by 38% on Outro. Therefore, he buffs Jiyan's damage by large amounts and has amazung synergy with him.

Mortefi is a good secondary for Absolution Phoebe with a Rejuvenating Glow Spectro Rover, however his Heavy ATK DMG Amplify on Outro faces loads of diminishing returns so his buffing potential mostly lies in his S6 and potentially the Static Mist pistol so he provides lots of ATK% to Phoebe. Overall this pairing is one of the best for Absolution Phoebe, but it is contested.

Mortefi, in Zani teams, acts as a substitute for Phoebe's buffing effects, but unfortunately doesn't apply any Spectro Frazzle. To compensate for this, Mortefi with Zani must be used with Spectro Rover, but under these conditions the team can work just fine and is able to clear endgame content without any issues, so the trio is definitely usable for F2P accounts!

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
